title: Drop the 2p rise in tax on savings interest
noun: dropping the rise in tax on savings interest
headline: Drop the savings rise. Costs £0.5bn in 2029-30.
description: From April 2027 savings interest above the allowances is taxed two percentage points higher at every rate. Switch this on to drop the rise.

baselinePolicy.text: Income tax on savings income is two percentage points higher at the basic, higher and additional rates from 6 April 2027 (Table 6.1 line 62).

source.quote: This measure increases the Basic, Higher and Additional rates of Income Tax on savings income by 2 percentage points.

alreadyIncludes: Income tax on savings income is two percentage points higher at the basic, higher and additional rates from 6 April 2027 (Table 6.1 line 62).

lines.title: Savings Income: Increase tax rates on savings income by 2ppts at the basic, higher and additional rate from 6 April 2027

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury’s costing with its sign reversed (positive scorecard values reduce borrowing; here receipts positive means more revenue).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.

interactions.text: Both change the rates on savings income: Budget 2025’s two points and this Budget’s two more.
